title: Vermont Statutes Annotated, Title 21 (Labor), Chapter 5 (Employment Practices), Subchapter 3A - Notice of Potential Layoffs Act
verified_how: fetched https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/chapter/21/005 (HTTP 200): headings 'Title 21 : Labor' and 'Chapter 005 : Employment Practices', subchapter heading 'Subchapter 003A : NOTICE OF POTENTIAL LAYOFFS ACT' listing s 411 (Definitions), 412 (Education and outreach), 413 (Notice and wage payment obligations), 414 (Exceptions), 415 (Violations), 416 (Powers of the Commissioner), 417 (Administrative penalty) and 418 (Other rights), none marked repealed. Every page of the Vermont Statutes Online carries the currency line 'The Statutes below include the actions of the 2025 session of the General Assembly.' and the caveat 'NOTE: The Vermont Statutes Online is an unofficial copy of the Vermont Statutes Annotated that is provided as a convenience.' No repeal marker appears on the cited provisions; repealed sections elsewhere in the same chapters are explicitly flagged 'Repealed. <act cite>', so the absence of that marker is meaningful.
notes: Vermont employment is at will and there is no general statutory severance-pay or individual-notice entitlement; this is Vermont's mini-WARN Act and the principal statute imposing notice and wage-payment duties on termination (mass layoff or closure). Related, verified on the same page: 21 V.S.A. s 306 (public policy of the State of Vermont; employment separation agreements) in Subchapter 1. Wage replacement after separation is 21 V.S.A. ch. 17 (Unemployment Compensation, ss 1301-1471), seen on the Title 21 index.
